proposed_widenings.name: container_object
proposed_widenings.justification: Bag of Holding is an enduring item with its own interior-capacity rules, contents, and object-local state. Current magic-item mechanics only cover passive grants, activated abilities, triggered reactions, and composites of those; none model a persistent container object.
proposed_widenings.evidence: This bag has an interior space considerably larger than its outside dimensions—roughly 2 feet square and 4 feet deep on the inside. The bag can hold up to 500 pounds, not exceeding a volume of 64 cubic feet. The bag weighs 5 pounds, regardless of its contents.

proposed_widenings.name: container_interaction
proposed_widenings.justification: The bag exposes repeatable object interactions like retrieving stored contents with a Utilize action, but those interactions are not resource-based activations and do not fit the current activation family honestly.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Retrieving an item from the bag requires a Utilize action.

proposed_widenings.name: container_air_supply
proposed_widenings.justification: The item tracks a finite breathable-air resource for creatures inside its extradimensional space. No current item header or mechanics family can represent shared internal air as persistent object state.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The bag holds enough air for 10 minutes of breathing, divided by the number of breathing creatures inside.

proposed_widenings.name: extradimensional_space_collision
proposed_widenings.justification: Placing the bag inside another extradimensional space causes a deterministic cross-item event: destroy both items, open a gate, and force nearby creatures through it. That is not a passive grant, activation, or triggered reaction on a creature.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Placing a Bag of Holding inside an extradimensional space created by a Handy Haversack, Portable Hole, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane.

proposed_widenings.name: gate_centered_area_exile
proposed_widenings.justification: The Astral-gate failure mode needs an area centered on a newly created gate location, then forced transport to a random Astral destination. Existing attachment families do not honestly express that item-created gate-centered event.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Any creature within a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on the gate is sucked through it to a random location on the Astral Plane.

notes: I did not author a Dhall/JSON content file because the unit's core mechanics are a persistent extradimensional container and cross-item failure mode, not an existing passive, activation, reaction, or composite magic-item shape.
